issues.description: ID generation uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure and could produce collisions
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a library like uuid for secure, collision-resistant IDs: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; return randomUUID();

issues.description: Email sanitization is not performed - only the name field is sanitized
issues.suggestion: Consider sanitizing the email field as well, or validate that it contains only expected characters after validation

issues.description: Email regex is basic and may not catch all edge cases (e.g., multiple @, international domains)
issues.suggestion: Consider using a more robust email validation library or extending the regex to handle edge cases. Alternatively, document that this is intentionally simplified.

issues.description: Error messages are plain strings - could benefit from error codes for better error handling
issues.suggestion: Create custom error classes with error codes: class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(code: string, message: string) { super(message); this.code = code; } }

issues.description: Database query is commented out - suggests incomplete implementation or test code
issues.suggestion: If this is production code, implement the actual database call. If it's a placeholder, add a TODO comment or inject the database connection as a dependency

codeQuality.summary: Overall excellent code quality with strong security practices. Found 1 medium issue regarding non-cryptographic random ID generation, 1 low priority maintainability concern, and 3 informational suggestions. The code demonstrates good practices: proper input validation, XSS prevention through sanitization, SQL injection prevention via parameterized queries, clear TypeScript typing, and good documentation. The main improvement would be using cryptographically secure ID generation.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is security-critical for preventing invalid data entry and potential injection attacks
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid email formats (user@example.com), invalid formats (no @, no domain, multiple @), edge cases (empty string, spaces, special chars like <script>@example.com), and Unicode characters

untestedPaths.reasoning: XSS prevention is security-critical. This function directly protects against cross-site scripting attacks
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test basic XSS patterns (<script>alert('xss')</script>), HTML entities (<>), attribute injection (onclick="alert()"), nested tags, and verify all dangerous characters are properly escaped. Test empty strings and strings without special chars.

Missing tests for security-critical functions (sanitizeInput, isValidEmail), business logic (createUser), and internal utilities (generateId, saveUser). Identified 11 untested paths including 2 critical, 5 high priority, 2 medium, and 2 low priority issues. Recommend starting with testing sanitizeInput and createUser functions as they handle security and core business logic.

suggestions.description: Extract magic numbers/strings and use a more robust ID generation approach
suggestions.benefits: Using a proper UUID library ensures better uniqueness guarantees and avoids potential collisions. If keeping custom implementation, extracting constants (36, 2, 9) improves maintainability and documents intent.

suggestions.description: Use established sanitization library instead of manual implementation
suggestions.benefits: Security-critical code should use battle-tested libraries like DOMPurify or html-escaper. Manual implementations may miss edge cases or encoding issues. Libraries handle Unicode, malformed input, and emerging attack vectors.

suggestions.description: Apply dependency injection for database operations to improve testability
suggestions.benefits: Enables easy unit testing by injecting mock repository. Follows SOLID principles (Dependency Inversion). Makes the function pure and easier to reason about. Allows switching database implementations without changing business logic.

suggestions.description: Extract input validation logic into dedicated validator function
suggestions.benefits: Improves single responsibility principle. Makes validation logic reusable and testable independently. Reduces createUser function complexity. Validation rules can be easily extended or modified in one place.

suggestions.description: Create custom error types for better error handling
suggestions.benefits: Allows callers to catch specific error types. Provides better error context with field information. Enables type-safe error handling. Makes it easier to distinguish between validation, database, and other errors.

suggestions.description: Simplify email validation by removing unnecessary variable
suggestions.benefits: Extracts regex as module-level constant for reusability. Eliminates regex recompilation on each call (minor performance improvement). Makes the pattern easier to test or modify separately.

suggestions.description: Consider using readonly properties for immutable fields
suggestions.benefits: Documents intent that id, email, and createdAt shouldn't be modified after creation. Provides compile-time safety against accidental mutations. Makes the interface contract clearer.

suggestions.description: Use object property shorthand where applicable
suggestions.benefits: Uses ES6 object property shorthand. Makes object construction more concise. Intermediate variables can be useful for debugging. Note: This is a stylistic choice - the original is also clean.

refactorings.summary: Found 8 refactoring opportunities for fixtures/clean-code.ts. High-impact suggestions include: using established sanitization libraries for security (high), applying dependency injection for testability (high), and extracting validation logic (medium). The code is already well-structured, so suggestions focus on production-readiness improvements like robust error handling, better dependency management, and using battle-tested libraries for security-critical operations.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive tests for security-critical functions sanitizeInput() and isValidEmail(). These functions protect against XSS and injection attacks but have zero test coverage.

Implement unit tests for createUser() function covering all validation branches (missing fields, invalid email format) and async error handling. This core business logic has 5 high-priority untested paths.
Replace manual HTML sanitization with battle-tested library (DOMPurify or html-escaper) to handle edge cases, Unicode, and emerging attack vectors that manual implementation may miss.
Apply dependency injection pattern to database operations (saveUser) to enable proper unit testing with mocked repositories and improve adherence to SOLID principles.
Replace Math.random() based ID generation with cryptographically secure alternative (crypto.randomUUID() or nanoid library) to prevent potential collisions and predictability issues.
